title: If the precept only bans absolute god-cult, it never touched the wise Gentiles’ relative simulacrum-cult
source_text: XLVII. Denique, si praecepto quo prohibemur facere & colere similitudinem ullam eorum quae sunt in coelo, vel in terra, vetamur solummodo imagines pro Diis habere, easque cultu absoluto, tanquam Deos colere, inde sequetur hoc praecepto non fuisse vetitum cultum simulachrorum a sapientibus gentium institutum. Ut enim jam indicavimus, disputationis hujus initio, distinguebant imagines a numinibus ipsis, nec eas colebant cultu absoluto, sed qui, ex colentium mente, referebatur ad numina, quorum ipsae simulachra erant.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, if by the commandment by which we are prohibited to make and cultivate any likeness of those things which are in heaven, or on earth, we are forbidden only to hold images for Gods, and to cultivate them with absolute cult, as Gods, then it will follow that by this commandment the cult of simulacra instituted by the wise of the Gentiles was not forbidden. For as we have already indicated at the beginning of this disputation, they distinguished images from the divinities themselves, nor did they cultivate them with absolute cult, but with that which, from the mind of the cultivators, was referred to the divinities of whom they themselves were simulacra.
pass_b_english: Narrow the precept to absolute god-cult and pagan sages walk free—they already distinguished sign from god.
Their relative referral is the same structure Rome now claims.
